hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, remember oxidation means an increase in oxidation number, so track each element from reactants to products.
Start with chromium and iron in FeCr2O4, using the clue that it contains Cr2O4 2- ions to find Fe is +2 and Cr is +3.
Now check what happens to carbon from carbonate to carbon dioxide, and see if its +4 oxidation number actually changes at all.
walkthrough:
**Find oxidation numbers in chromite**

Chromite is FeCr2O4 and contains Cr2O4 2- ions. Let Cr be x.

$$2x + 4(-2) = -2$$
This gives x = +3, so Cr is +3. For the whole FeCr2O4 to be neutral, Fe must be +2.

**Find oxidation numbers in the products**

In Na2CrO4, Na is +1 and O is -2, so Cr must be +6.

$$2(+1) + Cr + 4(-2) = 0$$
In Fe2O3, O is -2, so Fe must be +3. In both Na2CO3 and CO2, C is +4.

**Compare and decide who is oxidised**

Cr goes from +3 to +6, an increase, so it is oxidised. Fe goes from +2 to +3, an increase, so it is also oxidised.

C stays at +4 in both Na2CO3 and CO2, so it is not oxidised. Oxygen from O2 goes from 0 to -2, so it is reduced.

options.A: Correct. Both chromium (+3 to +6) and iron (+2 to +3) increase in oxidation number, so both are oxidised. Carbon stays at +4 and sodium stays at +1, so no other element is oxidised.
options.B: Incorrect. Carbon looks like it might change because CO2 is released, but its oxidation number is +4 in both $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$. No change means no oxidation.
options.C: Incorrect. Chromium is oxidised from +3 to +6, but it is not the only one. Iron is also oxidised from +2 in $\text{FeCr}_2\text{O}_4$ to +3 in $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$.
options.D: Incorrect. Iron is oxidised from +2 to +3, but chromium is also oxidised from +3 to +6 in $\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4$. This option misses the larger chromium change.
